figures.caption: Fig. 1. Confidence estimation across the clinical landscape, pooled over the five LVLMs. Rows are clinical categories (GMAI-MMBench by department, SLAKE by anatomical region, PATH-VQA by question type), sorted by base VQA accuracy, with a per-dataset summary row; GMAI-MMBench uses the shared question intersection common to all methods, SLAKE and PATH-VQA full coverage. Cells report AUROC, ECE, and safe yield at a 20 percent error tolerance (Y@20) on a green ramp, greener is better (for ECE, lower). All values are scaled to 0 to 100. Base accuracy and AUROC ramp together top to bottom, the capability-to-automatability gradient, and the trained probes read greener than the inference baselines in the lower-accuracy categories. Y@20 is a category’s own operating point in a category row but the single global threshold in a summary row, and the gap between the two, high in strong categories yet near zero pooled, is itself the finding: one global operating point suppresses automation that category-specific thresholds recover. Categories below 150 pooled cases are hatched, since per-category ECE is unstable on small strata.

TABLE I SELECTIVE PREDICTION (TRIAGE). AURC IS THE AREA UNDER THE RISK-COVERAGE CURVE (LOWER IS BETTER); YIELD@τ IS THE LARGEST AUTOMATABLE FRACTION HOLDING ERROR AMONG AUTOMATED CASES AT OR BELOW τ (AT LEAST 30 AUTOMATED CASES); ERRTOP10% IS THE ERROR RATE IN THE TOP CONFIDENCE DECILE. POOLED OVER (LVLM, QUESTION) PAIRS ACROSS THE FIVE LVLMS, SEED-AVERAGED FOR TRAINED PROBES. ORACLE IS A PERFECT-RANKING PREDICTOR; BEST PER COLUMN (EXCLUDING ORACLE) IN BOLD.
